input.paper_title: Graph-Aware Prompting for Reliable Section Generation
input.paper_venue: ACL Workshop on Natural Language Generation
input.paper_abstract: We present a graph-guided prompting workflow for long-form scientific writing that prioritizes evidence and citation consistency. Our method constructs a document graph that encodes section dependencies and uses strict JSON schemas and evidence-aware prompts to generate and validate individual sections. At generation time, the system (1) builds a section graph and schedules leaf-first writing, (2) retrieves and injects relevant evidence for each section, (3) produces JSON-constrained section outputs, and (4) assembles a LaTeX manuscript with refs.bib. We evaluate the approach by comparing it to a baseline linear prompting pipeline on two topical domains, measuring citation coverage, hallucination rate, and reviewer-style scores. Results show improved citation coverage and reduced unsupported assertions while keeping edits and post-hoc audits straightforward via machine-readable outputs. We intentionally state conservative claims and require explicit source citations for all factual assertions. The paper contributes practical artifacts: a graph-based section scheduler, an evidence-injection protocol per section, and an audit-friendly JSON output format that integrates with standard LaTeX/bib workflows. Our experiments use internal notes and a small curated PDF set where available; metrics focus on citation fidelity and factual consistency rather than broad generalization.

input.section_title: JSON schema, validation checks, and failure modes
input.section_summary: Define the JSON output schema for sections (fields, types, required citations), conservative validation rules (schema conformance, citation presence, evidence-consistency checks), automated repair attempts, and documented failure modes with fallback behaviors and audit traces.

output:
The following describes a proposed JSON output schema for individual manuscript sections, conservative validation checks that operate on generated section objects, automated repair attempts, and documented failure modes together with fallback behaviors and audit traces. This text presents a design proposal for the schema and validation protocol; where the presentation relies on common engineering heuristics or general practices rather than evidence excerpts, those items are explicitly labeled as ``general background knowledge.''

1. Design goals (explicit)
- Machine-readability: outputs must be parseable by downstream tooling (validators, assemblers, diff/audit tools).
- Citation provenance: every factual assertion that relies on external evidence should link to one or more provenance records so audits can trace assertions back to sources.
- Conservative acceptance: the validator should prefer rejection or human review to accepting outputs that lack required provenance.
- Repairability and traceability: any automated repair or transformation performed by the system must be recorded in an auditable trace attached to the section object.

2. JSON schema (proposed top-level fields)
- schema_version (string, required): identifier for the schema revision used to generate and validate the section.
- section_id (string, required): unique stable identifier for the section (e.g., ``sec:methods:2'').
- title (string, required): short human-readable title for the section.
- role (string, optional): one of a constrained set describing the section’s function (e.g., ``background'', ``methods'', ``result'', ``discussion''); presence aids graph-based scheduling and assembly.
- parent_ids (array[string], optional): identifiers of parent sections in the document graph.
- child_ids (array[string], optional): identifiers of children in the document graph.
- body (object, required): the substantive content of the section with structured subfields:
  - text (string, required): the primary content in a canonical format (preferably LaTeX or Markdown as determined by the pipeline configuration).
  - sentences (array[object], optional but recommended): tokenized/segmented sentences with per-sentence metadata; each sentence object may include:
    - sentence_id (string)
    - text (string)
    - assertions (array[object], optional): extracted assertion objects (see below)
- citations (array[object], required): list of citations referenced in the section; each citation object contains:
  - cite_key (string, required): bibliographic key to be used in refs.bib and manuscript assembly.
  - locator (string, optional): page/figure/table/paragraph locator when applicable.
  - provenance_ids (array[string], required): identifiers of retrieval artifacts (documents/snippets) that support this citation in this context.
  - evidence_snippet (string, optional): extracted supporting snippet (truncated) for quick inspection.
  - evidence_score (number, optional): retrieval/ranking score used for selection.
- assertions_index (array[object], optional but recommended): structured assertions extracted from the body with fields:
  - assertion_id (string)
  - text (string)
  - cited (boolean): whether the assertion has one or more linked citations
  - supporting_citation_keys (array[string]): cite_keys that support this assertion
  - supporting_provenance_ids (array[string]): provenance record ids
- metadata (object, required): generation metadata and validation state:
  - generator (string): model/version or process id that produced the section
  - generated_at (string, ISO-8601 timestamp)
  - validation_status (enum: ``unknown'',``passed'',``failed'',``repaired'',``requires_review'')
  - validation_errors (array[string]): human-readable error messages produced by validators
  - repair_attempts (array[object]): chronological log of automated repair attempts (see below)
  - audit_trace (array[object]): append-only trace of significant actions (validation results, repairs, human reviews)
- bib_entries (array[object], optional): generated minimal bib entries corresponding to cite_keys to facilitate immediate assembly; these should be reconciled with the global refs.bib during manuscript assembly.

3. Conservative validation checks (runtime rules)
The validator operates in stages. The checklist below enumerates conservative checks to be applied; each failing check yields a deterministic validation error message and sets validation_status accordingly.

A. Schema conformance
- Required fields present and of correct type (schema_version, section_id, title, body, citations, metadata).
- Canonical types for each field (e.g., citations is an array of objects). Failure: reject and attempt schema repair.

B. Citation presence and linkage
- Non-empty citations array for sections that contain factual content (policy: sections labeled as ``background'', ``methods'', ``results'', or ``discussion'' must include a citations array; exceptions require explicit human override).
- Every assertion marked as asserted in assertions_index must have at least one supporting_citation_keys entry.
- Every citation entry must include one or more provenance_ids.

C. Evidence-consistency checks
- For each citation listed, verify that at least one provenance_id resolves to an available retrieval artifact in the evidence cache (existence check).
- If evidence_snippet is provided, check that that snippet or a close substring appears among the injected evidence for the section (string containment or exact-match heuristic).
- Cross-check that the text of assertions does not contradict the content of the primary supporting snippet (conservative heuristic: flag potential contradictions where negations or numeric mismatches are detected). Note: the contradiction heuristic is a practical engineering heuristic (general background knowledge) and should be configured conservatively to minimize false positives.

D. Format safety
- Verify that the chosen body.text format is acceptable to downstream assemblers (e.g., only allowed LaTeX macros).
- Sanitize or reject any disallowed macros or embedded executables.

E. Provenance completeness
- Ensure metadata.provenance/audit fields are present and that validation_errors is initialized.

4. Automated repair attempts (ordered, auditable)
All automated repairs must append an entry to metadata.repair_attempts and audit_trace describing the operation, timestamp, and outcome.

- Type coercions: where a field is present but wrong-typed (e.g., citations provided as an object), attempt deterministic coercion (wrap single object into array). If coercion applied, record as ``coercion'' repair with before/after snapshot.
- Missing citation linkage: for assertions lacking supporting citations, automatically attempt a retrieval-based repair (general background knowledge): formulate a query from the assertion text, retrieve top-K candidate evidence snippets, and if any candidate’s retrieval score exceeds a conservative threshold, attach it as provenance and add/update citations accordingly. Record the retrieval query, candidate ids, scores, and the rule used to accept a candidate. If no candidate meets threshold, set validation_status to ``requires_review'' and add a human-review task.
- Missing bib entries: if cite_key referenced but corresponding bib_entries are missing, attempt to generate a minimal bib entry from provenance metadata (title/author/year) and mark it as provisional; record provenance of the generated bib entry.
- Sanitization repair: for disallowed formatting, perform minimal sanitization (escape or strip macros) and record the change. If automatic sanitization would substantially alter meaning, prefer ``requires_review.''

5. Failure modes and fallback behaviors
The validator and repair subsystem are designed to fail conservatively. The following failure modes should be explicitly tracked and their fallback behaviors are specified.

- Retrieval failure (no supporting provenance found)
  - Symptom: assertion or citation has empty or unresolved provenance_ids.
  - Fallback: set validation_status = ``requires_review'', attach a human-review task with the assertion text and the automated retrieval queries attempted. Audit_trace records attempted queries and retrieved candidates (if any).

- Evidence mismatch (provenance resolves but does not support the claim)
  - Symptom: evidence_snippet or provenance content contradicts the assertion according to heuristic checks.
  - Fallback: set validation_status = ``failed'' or ``requires_review'' depending on severity; optionally remove the offending citation and mark the assertion as unsupported. All actions logged in audit_trace.

- Hallucinated citation keys (cite_key present but no corresponding provenance)
  - Symptom: citation cite_key exists but provenance_ids are missing or provenance docs do not reference the claimed content.
  - Fallback: mark citation as provisional, attempt automated retrieval for the cited claim; if unsuccessful, flag for human intervention and do not include the provisional citation in final refs.bib without explicit approval.

- Schema incompatibility with assembly
  - Symptom: body format or field sets are incompatible with manuscript assembler.
  - Fallback: fail assembly step; validator returns deterministic error messages and suggested repairs; human-in-the-loop required before assembly.

- Propagated graph inconsistency
  - Symptom: parent/child relations contradict other sections’ ids or lead to cycles not allowed by scheduling rules.
  - Fallback: place affected sections into a ``graph_review'' queue; assembly proceeds only on a graph-consistent subgraph; graph inconsistency events are recorded in audit_trace.

6. Audit trace and human-review interface
- Record format: each audit_trace entry is an object with fields {timestamp, actor, action, inputs, outputs, decision, rationale, links_to_artifacts}.
- Human-review tasks: validators must produce compact review packages containing the section text, highlighted assertions lacking provenance, the attempted retrieval queries and top candidate snippets, and a one-click action set (accept-provisional, add-citation, edit-text, reject-section).
- Retention: maintain immutable audit_trace with versioned snapshots to allow later forensic inspection and to support reproducible rebuilds of the manuscript state.

7. Operational notes and conservative defaults (general background knowledge)
- Heuristic thresholds for accepting retrieved evidence into provenance should err on the side of higher precision (i.e., require higher scores) to reduce false attachments of weak evidence.
- NLP-based contradiction detection and assertion extraction are imperfect; therefore, their outputs must be treated as suggestions that trigger either automated conservative actions (e.g., set requires_review) or human verification.

8. Metrics to surface during validation (for operator dashboards)
- Counts of assertions without provenance, citations with unresolved provenance_ids, number of automated repairs applied, and sections in ``requires_review'' state. These are operational diagnostics; thresholds and alerting policies are configuration parameters.

9. Limitations of the schema and validation protocol
- This schema is a design artifact; it does not guarantee detection of all unsupported assertions or of all subtle citation mismatches. The contradiction and assertion-detection heuristics are approximate (general background knowledge) and should be calibrated per domain.
- Automated repair that attaches evidence counters the goal of conservative acceptance; therefore repairs are recorded and flagged as provisional until human verification completes.

10. Summary
The proposed JSON schema couples structured section content with explicit citation provenance, a conservative validation checklist, auditable automated repair attempts, and well-specified fallback behaviors for common failure modes. The design prioritizes traceability and human-in-the-loop resolution over blind acceptance of repaired outputs, enabling downstream assemblers and reviewers to inspect the provenance and validation history of each section before inclusion in the final manuscript.
